Sub: 
Proposals for Exemption/ Extension of Exemption from EDLI Scheme - 1976. 
Ref: 
a) This Office Circular dated 29.04.2021.
b) Appendix 
- 1 (All relevant Circulars). 
c) Appendix -2 (Girculars issued with direction for Class of Employees)
Madam/Sir,
It has been observed that various proposals regarding grant of exemption/ extension 
of Exemption from EDLI Scheme 1976 have been forwarded by field offices to Head Office for 
approval of CPFC. 
2 
In this regard, the following provisions governing the same are highlighted: 
Exemption to be granted under Section 17 (2A) stipulates the following:
The Central Provident Fund Commissioner may, if requested so to do by the employer, 
by notification in the Oficial Gazette, and subject to such conditions as may be specified in the 
notification, exempt, whether prospectively or retrospectively,any establishment from the 
operation of all or any of the provisions of the Insurance scheme, if he is satisfied] that the 
employees of such establishment are, without making any separate contribution or payment of 
premium, in enjoyment of benefits in the nature of lfe insurance, whether linked to their 
deposits in provident fiund or not, and such benefits are more favourable to such employees 
than the benefits admissible under the Insurance Scheme."

Exemption to be granted under Section 17 (2B) stipulates the following: 
"Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (2A), the Insurance Scheme may 
provide for the exemption of any person or dass of persons employed 
COvered by that scheme from the operation of all or any of the provisions thereof, if the benefits 
in the nature of life insurance admissible to such person, or class of persons are more 
favourable than the benefits provided under the insurance Scheme." 
any establishment and 
3. 
As is evident from the above, there is basic difference between the two provisions. 
Whereas, in the former, exemption is granted to establishment as a whole for which Central 
Provident Fund Commissioner is the competent authority, in the case of latter, it is granted to a 
class of employees 'or' employee(s) for which powers have been delegated to Additional Central 
Provident Fund Commissioner (HQS) or Addl. CPFC, as per Gazetted Notification {(G.S.R 
299(E)} dated 28.04.2021 (copy enclosed). 
4. 
Further, vide Circular dated 29.04.2021 (copy enclosed), it was also intimated that 
all such proposals for grant of exemption from EDLI Scheme, 1976 that may have been 
forwarded to HO are required to be re-examined by concerned office in the light of the above 
amendment. In the pending exemption proposals where the establishment may have sought 
exemption for a "class of employees ", where such class may be of regular employees of the 
establishment or any other such defined class, appropriate action for grant of exemption may 
be taken in accordance with relevant directions issued from time to time as mentioned under 
reference. Further, for ease of referencing, list of documents is also attached herevwith as 
in Appendix 2. 
It is, however, noticed that proposals for grant of exemption from EDLI Scheme 
1976 
5. 
are invariably being received in Head Office without clearly stating as to under which 
Section [17(2A) or 17(2B)] the exemption is sought. There could be cases that need not be 
referred to Head Office as the competent authority would be Additional Central Provident Fund 
Commissioner (HQs) or Addl. CPFC. In order to remove this confusion, the folowing instructions 
are issued for strict compliance: 
In all cases requiring approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Additional
Central Provident Fund Commissioner(HQs) or Addl. CPFC, shall enclose a certificate
under her/his signature that the exemption is to be granted under Section 17 (2A) of the 
Act and the establishment shall comply/is complying in respect of all categories and 
classes of employees including contractual and casual ones inits own EPF Code 
Number. 
i. 
In case the exemption is sought only for regular employees (or any other class of 
employees), it is to be treated as exemption for class of employees for which Zonal 
ACCs are competent authority. 
ii.

The ZO/ RO must, in all cases, also check and ensure the basic requirement, that 
the benefits under the policies of insurers opted for by the establishments are more favorable 
than the benefits given under the EDLI Scheme, 1976, is fulfilled before approving any proposa 
at their level. Similarly, in each case under Section 17(2A) requiring approval of CPFC, Zonal 
ACC shall enclose a cetificate that the benefits under the policy of insurer opted for by the 
establishment are more favourable than the benefits given under the EDLI Scheme, 1976 
6. 
7 
Further, in order to have regular monitoring and check on/of pending EDLI 
proposals at Head Office, a monthly report is hereby prescribed by way of Google spreadsheet 
(link pasted below) that may be updated by Zonal Offices by 5" of every month. The same is to 
be uploaded as 'NIL' if there is no pendency. The said list shall include both cases under Section 
17 (2A) as well as Section 17 (2B). 
"https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A6M-3nelF7e0-Mcm0ppYC 
UuPe4YjGSaDgYRp06L2NG/edit?usp=sharing " 
[This issues with the approval of CPFC.] 
Yours faithfully, 
Encl.: As above. 
D6 D2 
(Vishal Agarwal) 
Regional P.F.Commissioner-I (EDLI)

Sub: Certificate for Exemption / Extension in lieu of EDLI Scheme -1976. 
 
Madam / Sir, 
This is to certify that:- 
a) (Establishment name with PF Code No.) has sought exemption / Extension of Exemption 
under Section 17 (2A) of the EDLI Scheme-1976  and  is found fit for granting the same. 
b)  The above establishment is complying as a whole in respect of all categories and 
classes of employees including contractual and casual ones in its own PF Code No. 
c) The insurance benefits under the policy of insurer opted by the establishment are more 
favourable than the benefits under the EDLI Scheme-1976.
